chunks: Regarding a woman who bequeathed wealth for emancipation, hajj, and charity, but it was insufficient, he said: “Begin with hajj, for it is obligatory. Then if anything remains, assign a portion to charity and a portion to emancipation.”

key_terms.أَوْصَتْ: She made a bequest in her will
key_terms.حَجٍّ: Hajj, the pilgrimage, treated here as an obligatory duty
key_terms.طَائِفَةً: A portion or share allocated from what remains

ai.seo_question: If a deceased woman left an insufficient bequest for hajj, charity, and freeing slaves, which should be carried out first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the order of fulfilling a bequest when the available wealth is insufficient for all specified purposes. It prioritizes hajj because it is an obligation, then directs that any remainder be divided between charity and emancipation.
